examples: In the meanwhile, the surveyors carried the line three miles, which was no contemptible day's work, considering how cruelly they were entangled with briers and gallbushes.

senses.definition: During the time that something is happening, often specifically in a different place.
examples: There was a party going on downstairs. Meanwhile, I was reading a book.

quotes.text: Meanwhile Nanny Broome was recovering from her initial panic and seemed anxious to make up for any kudos she might have lost, by exerting her personality to the utmost. She took the policeman's helmet and placed it on a chair, and unfolded his tunic to shake it and fold it up again for him.
quotes.reference: 1963, Margery Allingham, chapter 19, in The China Governess: A Mystery, London: Chatto & Windus, →OCLC:

senses.definition: During an intervening time; from now until a future time.
examples: We’re going on holiday next month; meanwhile, keep working on the project.

quotes.text: The day may dawn when fair play, love for one's fellow men, respect for justice and freedom, will enable tormented generations to march forth triumphant from the hideous epoch in which we have to dwell. Meanwhile, never flinch, never weary, never despair.
quotes.reference: 1955 March 1, Winston Churchill, “Defence”, in parliamentary debates (House of Commons), column 1905:

quotes.text: “[…] I’m not ignoring you, I’m very sorry, I’ll talk to you soon. Meanwhile, get your tickets.”

senses.definition: In contrast to aspects previously mentioned.
examples: Some songs on the album are beautiful. Meanwhile, others are quite forgettable.

quotes.text: When you are in the studio you don’t have anybody to feed off of, meanwhile when you are playing live you interact with people and you feel the energy in the room.
